input.summary: Propose a small emulated netem pilot comparing TCP flow completion time under 0 ms vs 20 ms added one-way delay, using two clients over a fixed bottleneck. The claim is nondirectional ("changes"), so both directions of effect count. This is a new-measurement simulation pilot; it cannot establish causality or generalize beyond the emulated conditions.
questions: Does the 20 ms delay in the claim refer to one-way or round-trip added latency in the netem emulation?
What bottleneck link rate (Mbit/s) and buffer size (kbytes) should be held fixed across conditions?
What file transfer size(s) should each client use, and which TCP congestion control algorithm(s) should be tested?

proposal.problem: It is unknown whether adding 20 ms of emulated delay meaningfully changes TCP flow completion time under fixed bottleneck conditions. The claim is nondirectional and the direction, magnitude, and CCA sensitivity are all untested.
proposal.question: Does adding 20 ms of emulated delay (vs. 0 ms baseline) produce a detectable change in TCP flow completion time under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Two delay conditions: 0 ms added delay (baseline) and 20 ms added delay (treatment). All other bottleneck parameters held fixed. Delay interpretation (one-way vs. round-trip) and bottleneck rate/buffer are unresolved and must be confirmed before freezing.
proposal.related_work: No full-text source was provided; the claim is synthetic. No prior measurements or citations are available to review.
proposal.alternatives: The delay effect may be negligible for small transfers, may interact with CCA choice (e.g., BBR vs. CUBIC), or may only manifest above a threshold file size. These are untested mechanisms, not reviewed findings.
proposal.design: Emulated netem pilot with two configurations (0 ms and 20 ms delay), two clients per run, fixed bottleneck rate and buffer, replicated across multiple runs. Flow completion time recorded per client per run.
proposal.metrics: Primary metric: flow_completion_time_ms (ms) per client. Compare distributions across delay conditions using a nonparametric test (e.g., Mann-Whitney U) given small sample size.
proposal.controls: Bottleneck rate, buffer size, file size, CCA, number of clients, and snapshot interval held constant across conditions. Only delay varies.
proposal.falsification: The claim is falsified if the distributions of flow completion time under 0 ms and 20 ms delay are indistinguishable (e.g., Mann-Whitney p > 0.05 and effect size negligible). Overlap in distributions does not establish no effect; it only fails to reject the null at this pilot scale.
proposal.inputs: Built-in netem runner (emulated-netem-v1). Bottleneck rate, buffer size, file size, and CCA must be specified by the owner before protocol can be frozen. Source SHA256 retained from paper_claim.
proposal.limitations: Emulated conditions may not reflect real network behavior. Pilot scale (small replication count) limits statistical power. One-way vs. round-trip delay interpretation is unresolved. Results cannot be generalized beyond the specific emulated configuration.
